entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Nitin Gupta - Government Advocate for respondent N
 Order

This is first criminal appeal filed by the appellant under Section 14(A)(2) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.645/2017 dated 04.12.2017 registered at Police Station City Kotwali, District Rewa for the offences punishable under Sections 366, 376(2(n), 506 of IPC and Section 3(2)(va) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
2. Counsel for appellant contended that allegations pertain to incident dated 03.12.2017 which according to the prosecution had taken place almost 8 years back.

It is further contended by the counsel that as per the allegations so levelled by the prosecution, it is evident that prosecutrix, who was a major lady, on her own volition came alongwith the present appellant and thereafter, there was physical relationship between them which was apparently consensual, therefore, the subsequent implication of present appellant is merely an afterthought and on the basis of such implication, the present appellant cannot be kept behind the bars for an indefinite period.
Thus, it is prayed that appellant be enlarged on bail.
The prayer is opposed by counsel for State and it is contended that in the present case, there are direct allegations against the appellant for commission of rape.

Considering the allegations which Mahendra Mishra @ Chunnu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157160181/
1 contain direct allegations, the appellant is not entitled for bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4. Heard submissions and perused the case diary.
5.

Taking into consideration the totality of the circumstances of the case coupled with the facts that there were consensual relationship between the appellant and the prosecutrix, prosecutrix was a major lady and appellant is in custody since 24/01/2025, this Court deems it proper to release the appellant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, the appeal is allowed.

6. It is directed that the appellant shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of trial.
7. It is further directed that the appellant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480 (3) of Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE vc Mahendra Mishra @ Chunnu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157160181/
